slice: Used-bike buying pass (2026-11-07, reviewed the same day): where the VIN and engine number are on Japanese-brand roster bikes (Kawasaki, Yamaha, Honda, Suzuki), and the RM-Z450 shifting complaint as a used-buyer check. Suzuki had no known_issues records before this pass. Recalls are not repeated here.

records.statement: Kawasaki says the VIN on its motorcycles is stamped on the steering head, below the handlebars. On a used KX, read it there yourself and compare it, character by character, with the title or bill of sale; Kawasaki US VINs begin JKA or JKB.

values.vin_location: stamped on the steering head, below the handlebars
values.wmi: JKA or JKB (seen in Kawasaki's own US VIN filings and recall VIN ranges)

source.name: Kawasaki parts site, how to identify your vehicle (VIN finder)

records.notes: General Kawasaki motorcycle statement, not a KX-specific manual page. The engine-number location was not confirmed from a Kawasaki document in this pass. JKA/JKB prefixes appear in Kawasaki's 2019 VIN filings (on-road models, https://vpic.nhtsa.dot.gov/mid/home/displayfile/39cbd4aa-de4b-4320-b68a-6994c6512ec7) and in the 2025 KX450 recall VIN ranges in kawasaki.json.

records.topic: Yamaha YZ: VIN on the steering head, model label on both sides
records.statement: The US regulator's notice for the 2022 YZ125 says the VIN is stamped on the frame steering head and the model number is printed on both sides of the bike. Yamaha's own older YZ450F owner's service manual (2016) puts the VIN on the right side of the frame and the engine serial number on the raised part of the right side of the engine.

values.vin_location: stamped on the frame steering head
values.model_label: printed on both the right and left sides
values.engine_number_2016_yz450f: stamped into the elevated part of the right side of the engine

source.name: CPSC recall notice 22-746 (Yamaha Motor Corporation USA), 2022 YZ125

records.notes: Recorded against the only roster bike the notice names. The 2016 YZ450F manual page (https://www.manualslib.com/manual/1161595/Yamaha-Yz450f.html?page=19) is outside the roster years and is given for the engine number only. The notice quotes the VIN range as ***CE34C***000301-004096, so recall notices may quote only part of a VIN. The recall itself is ki6-013.

records.topic: used RM-Z450: missed shifts and false neutrals
records.statement: Owners of 2014-on RM-Z450s, including the 2018-on generation, report missed shifts and false neutrals, most often 2nd to 3rd under hard acceleration; several blame the short stock shift lever and fix it with a longer one, and one bike needed gears and shift forks replaced. On a used RM-Z450, shift through every gear under load on the test ride and ask whether the gearbox has been opened.

values.test_ride: hard upshifts 2-3 and 3-4 under load; downshifts; note any neutral between gears
values.owner_fixes: longer or aftermarket shift lever (most common); stiffer shift-drum follower spring kit; one case needed 2nd-5th gears and shift forks

source.name: Vital MX forum thread on 2018 RM-Z450 faults

records.notes: In the 2019 thread (all posts 2019-04-10) two posters report shifting trouble: a friend's 2018 hit false neutrals and was having its transmission rebuilt at 44 hours, and another says a different shift lever helps a lot; a third suggests a longer lever. A 2017 thread on 2014-2016 bikes agrees (https://vitalmx.com/forums/Tech-Help-Race-Shop,42/14-and-newer-RMZ450-shifting,1314043, Feb-Mar 2017): about three owners report false neutrals, mostly 2nd to 3rd under hard acceleration, four recommend a longer lever, and one owner's 2015 had 2nd-5th gears and the shift forks replaced at about 5 hours; one says his 2017 is much better. Four owners in the 2019 thread report no problems at all. No report read for 2020-2025 bikes specifically; applied to them because the 2018-on engine and gearbox carried over, so confidence is low. Not a Suzuki bulletin. Re-read 2026-11-07.

records.topic: Honda CRF: where the VIN and engine number are
records.statement: Honda's 2020 owner's manuals put the VIN on the right side of the steering head on both the CRF250R/RX and the CRF450R/RX, but the engine number on different sides: the left crankcase on the CRF250R/RX and the right crankcase on the CRF450R/RX. On a used CRF, read both numbers off the bike and match them to the paperwork; US Honda VINs begin JH2.

values.vin_location: stamped on the right side of the steering head
values.wmi: JH2 (Honda Motor Co., motorcycle; NHTSA vPIC)

source.name: Honda 2020 CRF250R/RX owner's manual 31K95620, vehicle identification page

records.notes: CRF450R side from Honda's 2020 CRF450R/RX/RWE owner's manual 31MKE630 (https://2rom-prd-data.hondamotopub.com/om/AHM/CRF450RX-R-RWE/2020/CRF450R.RX.RWE_31MKE630_0.pdf, page 172, dated 2019-04-03), already held as p6h-017. This settles the earlier conflict: the left-crankcase reading in an older CRF450R edition matches the CRF250R layout, so the side depends on the model and possibly the generation. Honda's 2025 European CRF250R manual shows the frame and engine numbers only in a drawing. WMI from https://vpic.nhtsa.dot.gov/api/vehicles/DecodeWMI/JH2?format=json. Read 2026-11-07.

records.topic: Suzuki RM-Z: where the frame and engine numbers are
records.statement: Suzuki's RM-Z450 owner's service manual (2008 edition) says the frame number is stamped on the steering head and the engine serial number on the right side of the crankcase. Later RM-Z owner's service manuals keep a serial number location page; check the one for the bike's year. US Suzuki VINs begin JS1.

values.vin_location: stamped on the steering head (2008 RM-Z450 manual)
values.engine_number: stamped on the right side of the crankcase (2008 RM-Z450 manual)
values.wmi: JS1 (Suzuki Motor Corporation, motorcycle; NHTSA vPIC)

source.name: Suzuki RM-Z450 (K8) owner's service manual, serial number location

records.notes: The only Suzuki document whose serial-number page could be read in this pass is for the 2008 RM-Z450, twelve or more years before these bikes; a 2021 RM-Z250 owner's manual listing shows a SERIAL NUMBER LOCATION heading but its text was not readable, and one manual site sits behind a bot check, which was not worked around. Applied with low confidence: steering-head frame numbers are the norm, but the crankcase side is not confirmed for current bikes. WMI from https://vpic.nhtsa.dot.gov/api/vehicles/DecodeWMI/JS1?format=json. Read 2026-11-07.

conflicts.detail: Several owners report false neutrals; most owners in the same thread report none, and one says the 2017 was much improved.

Resolved in review: Honda's 2020 manuals put the engine number on the left crankcase of the CRF250R and the right crankcase of the CRF450R; an older CRF450R edition says left. The side depends on the model (and possibly the generation), so riders are told to check the manual for the exact bike.

not_found: Kawasaki KX engine-number location from a Kawasaki document.
Reliable Suzuki RM-Z250 2020-2027 weak spots: the per-year 'common issues' pages found were generic and in places wrong (one calls the fuel-injected 2021 RM-Z250 carbureted), so they were not used.
Suzuki RM-Z owner's service manual for 2020-2027 with a readable serial-number page (the 2008 RM-Z450 one is used, low confidence).

Suzuki RM-Z250 weak spots: a 2024 owners' thread (https://www.vitalmx.com/forums/moto-related/rmz250-reliability, 2024-04-02) and a 2019 RM-Z250 build thread (https://www.vitalmx.com/comment/3776840, 2020-04) report no recurring failure; only single-owner gripes (hot clutch free play, brake fade), so nothing was recorded.

RM-Z450 clutch judder springs: owners remove them for a crisper, drag-free engagement (https://www.vitalmx.com/forums/Tech-Help-Race-Shop,42/19-rmz450-Judder-spring-removal,1372274, 2020-2025); a modification, not a fault, so not recorded.
